paragraphs: Derbyshire County Council runs its own fostering service and is part of Foster for East Midlands Councils, a partnership of councils that aims to keep children in their own communities, near family and friends, with training and ongoing support for carers. Children from the county may also live with independent agencies such as those listed on this page.
The council says it needs more homes for children in care, with carers wanted for children of all ages and abilities, including disabled children and brothers and sisters.

You need to be over 21 and have a spare room; there is no upper age limit and no qualifications are required. In a March 2026 article the council said that single people, renters and people in social housing, working people, LGBTQ+ people and people with a disability can all foster. Smoking or vaping is assessed case by case, with tighter limits for children under five, parent and child placements and children with breathing conditions. Most pets are fine apart from banned dog breeds. You do not have to drive, but you need reliable transport for school, health appointments and family time, and minor or old convictions are looked at individually.

The council also holds drop-in events where you can talk to current foster carers and their families. Before deciding, compare what the council offers with two or three of the agencies below, and ask each about pay, training and support near you.
